summary: George Berrington ran the opening session with Chris Barlow and Leanne Morris to pin down who Meridian should be selling to. We agreed the core ICP is PE-backed UK manufacturers with £20m to £150m revenue in the first 18 months after acquisition. Positioning will move away from generic lean consulting towards value-creation plan delivery for operating partners.

discussion.keyPoints: Chris said roughly 70% of fees in the last two years came from three PE houses. Leanne flagged that this concentration is a risk if one operating partner moves firm.

Best margins and fastest decisions come on 100-day plans after a buy-out, where operating partners need shop-floor improvements quickly. Generic lean training work is slow to close and price sensitive.
Leanne listed the big-four operations teams and two regional lean boutiques. Chris felt Meridian loses on brand to the big firms but wins on speed of mobilisation and hands-on delivery.

recommendations.recommendation: Target PE-backed UK manufacturers with £20m to £150m revenue within 18 months of acquisition, with the operating partner as the economic buyer.
Position Meridian as the team that delivers the operational lines of the value-creation plan, mobilising a team on site within 10 working days.
Add mid-market PE houses with fewer than 15 portfolio companies as a second segment, aiming to open 5 new PE relationships in 12 months.
Stop quoting day rates on 100-day plans and quote a fixed fee per workstream starting at £45k.

actions.action: Pull fee data by client and sector for the last 24 months
List every operating partner Meridian has worked with since 2022

nextFocus: Turn the agreed ICP into a value proposition and commercial narrative for operating partners.
nextPreparation: Leanne to bring three recent win stories with the before and after numbers.

tests.question: What did we agree our ICP is?
Is the fixed-fee pricing for 100-day plans agreed yet?
